source_refs.note: Topic 1.7.6, printed page 13: the definition of electronegativity, Pauling's scale and the factors.

blocks.title: Electronegativity
blocks.text: Electronegativity is the power of an atom to attract the shared pair of electrons towards itself in a molecule.

Linus Pauling, an American chemist, developed a scale of dimensionless electronegativity values, ranging from just below one for the alkali metals to a maximum of four for fluorine. Higher values signify a stronger attraction for electrons.

items: Atomic size: a larger atom has a lower electronegativity, because electrons far from the nucleus feel a weaker attraction. The halogens of group 17 run F greater than Cl greater than Br greater than I.

Effective nuclear charge: a higher effective nuclear charge gives a greater electronegativity, because the increased charge attracts the bonded electrons more strongly; this is why electronegativity rises across a period. Lithium in period 2 has 1.0 and fluorine 4.0.

blocks.title: Did you know
blocks.text: Linus Pauling is the only person to have received two unshared Nobel Prizes: chemistry in 1954 for his work on the nature of the chemical bond, and peace in 1962 for his opposition to weapons of mass destruction.
